summary: IonQ is the revenue leader in listed quantum computing (Q2 revenue $80.1M, +287% YoY, about two-thirds of the listed pure-play group's Q2 revenue) and has raised 2026 guidance to $450–460M after closing the SkyWater foundry deal. At $45.30 (≈$18B market cap, ≈$16B EV) it trades far below pure-play peers on EV/Sales but far above anything a cash-flow model can justify, with ~$484M TTM free-cash burn and 50% share-count growth in a year. Triangulating peer multiples, a 2030 earnings-power DCF and the analyst range gives a fair value of roughly $36–60 (mid $48), so the stock looks fairly valued with wide error bars. Stay Neutral; options IV (~70%) sits near a 52-week low and below 30-day realized vol (~81%), which favors defined-risk long-premium structures over outright stock.

valuation.method: Equal-weight triangulation. (a) Peer multiples: 20–35x NTM EV/Sales (a discount to RGTI/QBTS because of low-margin foundry mix) × ≈$687M NTM revenue implied by the 26.3x forward P/S, plus $2.06B net cash, over 397.3M shares → $40–66. (b) 2030 earnings-power DCF: revenue $1.6B base / $2.5B bull at 8–10x EV/Sales, discounted 4 years at 15%, plus ≈$0.8B net cash after burn, over ≈420M diluted shares → $19–36. (c) Analysts: low $35–42, median $65, high $100. Blended mid ≈ $48; range $36–60.
valuation.note: No P/E is meaningful for the quantum pure-plays, since all are loss-making. IBM is shown as the profitable scale competitor. The valuation depends heavily on whether fault-tolerant systems arrive in 2027–28 on schedule; the DCF leg alone says the stock is expensive.
